ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that there is an equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$, point $D$ is on the outside of $AC$, $BD$ is rotated clockwise by $60^\circ$ around point $B$ to $BF$, point $F$ corresponds to point $D$, connect $AF$, $AD$, with $AD=2$, $\angle CBD=15^\circ$, and $\angle AFB=30^\circ$, then what is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \quad \text{As shown in the figure, connect } DF, \text{ extend } FA \text{ to intersect } BD \text{ at } E, \]
\[ \because BD \text{ rotates clockwise around point } B \text{ by } 60^\circ \text{ to } BF, \]
\[ \therefore BD = BF, \angle DBF = 60^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle BDF \text{ is an equilateral triangle, } \angle BFD = 60^\circ. \]
\[ \because \angle BFA = 30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle DFA = 30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore FE \text{ perpendicularly bisects } BD, \]
\[ \therefore AD = AB, \]
\[ \because \angle ABC = 60^\circ, \angle CBD = 15^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABD = 45^\circ \]
\[ \therefore \triangle DAB \text{ is an isosceles right triangle, } \]
\[ \therefore DE = AE = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AD = \sqrt{2}, \]
\[ \therefore BD = DF = 2\sqrt{2} \]
\[ \therefore EF = \sqrt{DF^{2} - DE^{2}} = \sqrt{6} \]
\[ AF = EF - AE = \boxed{\sqrt{6} - \sqrt{2}}. \]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, B is at the lower right, C is at the lower left, A is in the upper middle, and ABC forms an equilateral triangle; D is on the left side, located outside AC; F is above, and the line segments BF, AF, AD, BD, AC, BC have been drawn. According to the positions in the figure, viewed from B, ray BD is located between BA and BC; viewed from F, if DF is connected, then ray FA is located between FB and FD. Extending FA downward will intersect BD; denote the intersection point by E, and the position of the figure shows that A is between F and E. Then reason: connect DF, and extend FA to intersect BD at E. Because BD is rotated clockwise by 60° about B to obtain BF, so BD=BF, ∠DBF=60°, hence △BDF is an equilateral triangle, and ∠BFD=60°. Also it is known that ∠AFB=30°, and FA is inside ∠BFD, so ∠DFA=60°−30°=30°, that is, FE is the angle bisector of vertex angle F in the equilateral triangle BDF. Therefore FE is also the altitude and median of BD, so FE perpendicularly bisects BD. Since A is on FE, A is on the perpendicular bisector of BD, obtaining AD=AB. It is known that AD=2, therefore AB=2. Also △ABC is an equilateral triangle, so ∠ABC=60°; in the figure BD is between BA and BC, and ∠CBD=15°, so ∠ABD=60°−15°=45°. In △ABD, AD=AB, so the base angles ∠ABD=∠BDA=45°, thus ∠DAB=90°, and △ABD is an isosceles right triangle. Hence the hypotenuse BD=2√2, and E is the midpoint of BD, so DE=√2; at the same time, in this isosceles right triangle, AE=√2. Also △BDF is equilateral, so DF=BD=2√2. In the right triangle DEF, EF=√(DF²−DE²)=√((2√2)²−(√2)²)=√(8−2)=√6. Since A is located between F and E, AF=EF−AE=√6−√2. Final answer: AF=√6−√2.
